findings.declaration: DiagonalCoordinateRing.relation (and its uses in quotient_offDiagonal and ideal_isHopfIdeal_proof)
findings.excerpt:
def relation (i j : ι) : GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K ι :=
  if i = j then 0 else matrix K ι i j
findings.problem: `relation` is a bare `def` with an `if` body and no equation lemmas for its two cases. Every proof that uses it unfolds the definition and then fixes up the `if`. `quotient_offDiagonal` does `simpa [relation, h] using hz`. Inside `ideal_isHopfIdeal_proof`, `counit_gen`, `comul_gen` and `antipode_gen` each repeat `simp [relation, hij]` for the diagonal case and `simp only [relation, hij, ite_false]` for the off-diagonal case. The same unfold-and-split pattern appears six times. `relation` is not marked `@[simp]` or `@[reducible]`, so `simp` leaves `relation K ι i j` as an opaque term. Callers must know the `if` implementation to reduce it.
findings.proposed_change: Add two equation lemmas right after the definition. These are `@[simp] theorem relation_self (i) : relation K ι i i = 0 := by simp [relation]` and `@[simp] theorem relation_of_ne {i j} (h : i ≠ j) : relation K ι i j = matrix K ι i j := by simp [relation, h]`. Then the six occurrences can drop `relation` from the simp set. The off-diagonal case becomes `rw [relation_of_ne hij]` (or `simp [hij]`), and the diagonal case becomes `simp [hij]` or `subst hij; simp`. The definition is unfolded in one place only and the `ite_false` plumbing disappears. If later files such as `UpperTriangularCoordinateRing.lean` reuse this pattern with their own `relation`, they can follow the same shape.
findings.benefit: `relation` gets a canonical simp normal form, so proofs about the ideal generators no longer depend on the `if` implementation. `simp` reduces `relation K ι i i` to `0`, and `relation K ι i j` to a matrix entry once `i ≠ j` is known, so the three Hopf-ideal side goals share one reduction step.

findings.declaration: DiagonalCoordinateRing.quotient (opaque def) with simp lemmas quotient_offDiagonal / universal_apply
findings.excerpt:
def quotient : GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K ι →ₐ[K] CoordinateRing K ι :=
  Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K (ideal K ι)
findings.problem: The simp interface is stated in terms of the plain `def` `quotient`, but no lemma connects `quotient` to `Ideal.Quotient.mk (ideal K ι)`. Mathlib lemmas such as `Bialgebra.Quotient.counit_mk` and the `Ideal.Quotient` API are phrased with `Ideal.Quotient.mk`, and `simp` cannot see through `quotient`. Downstream users therefore reach for `change` to convert by defeq. `UpperTriangularSplitKernel.lean` does `change Coalgebra.counit (R := K) (Ideal.Quotient.mk (UpperTriangularCoordinateRing.ideal K n) ...) = ... (Ideal.Quotient.mk (DiagonalCoordinateRing.ideal K n) ...)` before `rw [Bialgebra.Quotient.counit_mk, ...]`. The same file repeats long `change` blocks around `quotient` at lines 211–217, 242–259 and 329–333. Inside this file, `ideal_isHopfIdeal_proof` also uses `change Coalgebra.counit ...`, `change (Algebra.TensorProduct.map q q) ...` and `change q (...)` to get from `quotient` to the Mathlib forms. `quotient_offDiagonal` has the extra hypothesis `h : i ≠ j`, and `simp` only discharges it when `hij : ¬ i = j` or `i ≠ j` is a simp argument. Users still call it with `rw [...quotient_offDiagonal K n i index h ...]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a defeq-proved bridge lemma `theorem quotient_apply (x) : quotient K ι x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (ideal K ι) x := rfl`. Do not make it a global `@[simp]` lemma, because it would rewrite away the `quotient (matrix ..)` form that `quotient_offDiagonal` and `universal_apply` match. Together with it, add simp-usable companions in the `quotient` normal form for the Hopf operations used in this file and its consumers. Examples are `counit (quotient x) = counit x` and `Algebra.TensorProduct.map (quotient) (quotient) (comul x)`, if they hold by `Bialgebra.Quotient` lemmas. Callers can then `rw [quotient_apply]` or `simp [quotient_apply]` instead of the `change ... Ideal.Quotient.mk ...` blocks.
findings.benefit: Callers no longer need long `change` statements that restate both sides in `Ideal.Quotient.mk` form. They can use Mathlib's quotient-Hopf simp lemmas directly, and the simp set around `quotient` is predictable.
